draft.title: Light-dependent and light-independent stages
card: happens in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast. Chlorophyll absorbs light energy, which splits water and releases oxygen.
The light energy is stored in ATP and NADPH. These are energy carriers that move to the next stage.
is the Calvin cycle, in the stroma. It uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon: carbon dioxide is built into sugar, with the enzyme Rubisco starting the process.
The Calvin cycle does not use light directly. It still depends on the ATP and NADPH made using light, so it slows when light-dependent supply stops.
draft.remember: Thylakoids capture light as ATP and NADPH. The stroma spends them to build sugar.

a.q: Which pair of products of the light-dependent stage is used by the Calvin cycle?
a.why: The light-dependent stage stores light energy in ATP and NADPH, and the Calvin cycle spends them. Glucose is made by the Calvin cycle, not passed to it. Oxygen is released and is not used by the cycle.
a.clue: Think of the energy carriers passed from thylakoid to stroma.

b.q: Researchers move a leaf into darkness. The Calvin cycle in its chloroplasts soon stops making sugar. What is the best explanation?
opts: No new ATP and NADPH are being made in the thylakoids
Rubisco cannot work once chlorophyll is in the dark
Carbon dioxide cannot enter the stroma without light
Water is no longer split to supply carbon for sugar
b.why: Without light, the thylakoids stop making ATP and NADPH, so the Calvin cycle runs out of energy supply. The Calvin cycle is called light-independent because it uses no light directly, but it still needs these products. Chlorophyll does not act on Rubisco.
b.clue: The Calvin cycle needs what the thylakoids supply.

b.best: No new ATP and NADPH are being made in the thylakoids
